messages:
olivia_support: FYI customer `acme-inc` reporting intermittent 429s + p95 token latency spikes from their dedicated pool (eu-west-1 / pool-3) starting ~03:40 UTC. They see `rate_limited` on some requests and large tail latency. Suspect noisy neighbor / MIG contention.

maya_oncall: Can you paste a sample request id and the tenant allocation? Also did autoscale trigger?

olivia_support: sample request id: `req_0a7f3b9c`. Tenant allocation: pool-3 -> node-187 (MIG slices: 7g.1, 7g.2). Autoscale-bot shows no successful scale up during spike window.

maya_oncall: ok thanks. Can infra grab host-level metrics (nvidia-smi, nvml counters) and tenant-level qps during the spike? If MIG sibling is pegged on SM/utilization that would explain kernel contention.

dmitri_infra: pulled logs from node-187 for 03:30-04:10 UTC. Dropping the relevant snippet: ```
Timestamp, MIG, SM%, Mem%, SM Util spike
03:38:54, 7g.1, 96, 78, 95
03:39:02, 7g.2, 7, 20, 8
03:39:10, 7g.1, 97, 79, 96
03:41:01, 7g.1, 99, 82, 98
```
Looks like 7g.1 is saturating SM while 7g.2 is idle. Also observed repeated CUDA kernel queueing and increased driver NVML 'gpu_busy' counters for 7g.1.

olivia_support: nice find. Customer also provided a small repro that sends repeated small gen requests (seq_len ~ 32, batch=1). That workload is latency-sensitive and gets hit by co-located heavy batched requests.

maya_oncall: two paths: 1) live-migrate tenant to a node with empty MIG slices (fast mitigation), 2) throttle the aggressive tenant on that node or adjust autoscale to prefer padding spare nodes. For immediate relief I recommend migration.

autoscale-bot: [autoscale] node-187 autoscale attempt at 03:40:12 failed -> reason: capacity constraint; current free MIG slices: 0.

admin_ops: initiated admin-migrate-tenant --tenant acme-inc --from node-187 --to node-202 (preferred empty host) at 03:45 UTC. Command output: ```
[START] migrate acme-inc
drain connections on 7g.1
move KV cache for session prefixes
attach to node-202: success
[OK] migration complete in 22s
```

olivia_support: after migration customer reports p95 dropped from ~1.2s to 110ms and 429s stopped. Confirmed with telemetry.

dmitri_infra: follow-up root cause: neighbor tenant on 7g.1 was running a long batched reranking job with sustained SM saturation (non-quantized kernels). We'll file infra action to: (a) add an SM throttling guard for batched jobs on shared MIG hosts, (b) update scheduling to avoid colocating latency-sensitive tenants with sustained compute batches.

admin_ops: created ticket OPS-4821 to evict/retire noisy workloads and update placement heuristics.

olivia_support: marked incident as mitigated. Customer notified and given migration timeline + billing note (no billing break).

sarah_support: thanks team, closing thread after follow-up with product for scheduling policy. :white_check_mark:
